 Judgment

Both appeals are arising out common judgment dated 04th April, 2022 passed in MVC No.104 and 105 of 2020 by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Hubballi (for short, hereinafter referred to as "Tribunal").

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in these appeals are referred to with their rank and status before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 04th December, 2019 at about 12.45 am, deceased Manjunath was proceeding on motorcycle bearing No.KA-63/J-9610 along with pillion rider Vishwanath on Hubballi-Dharwad by-pass road near Rayanal bridge.

At that time, the bus bearing registration No.KA-57/F- 3594 belonging to KSRTC coming from Dharwad being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, losing control over the bus, went to extreme right side and dashed to the motorcycle.
Resultantly, the rider and pillion rider of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:11019-DB motorcycle sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same.

4. Pursuant to notice issued by the Tribunal, the respondent No.1-KSRTC appeared through its Advocate and filed objections in which it is stated that the motorcycle was driven in drunken state and without valid driving licence and the rider of the motorcycle himself was responsible for accident.
Hence, respondent-KSRTC is not liable to pay any compensation.
The owner and insurer of the motorcycle are also necessary parties to the petition.
The bus was duly insured.
Further the averments made in the claim petition are denied as false and sought for dismissal of claim petition.

5. Respondent No.2-Insurance Company appeared and filed similar objections contending that the rider of the motorcycle was himself negligently riding the motorcycle and without driving licence that too in a drunken state and he himself is responsible for the accident for which the respondent No.2 cannot be made liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.2 also denied all other averments made in the claim petition and sought for its dismissal.

Based on the rival pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues for its consideration:
1.

Whether the petitioners proves that on 04.12.2019 at about 12-45 a.m. night near Rayanal bridge, Hubballi- Dharwad bypass, Hubballi, when the deceased motor cyclist along with pillion rider were proceeding on motor cycle bearing No.KA-63/J- 9610 then the bus bearing No.KA-63/F- 3594 belonging to respondent No.1, insured with respondent No.2 driven by its driver in high speed, rash or negligent manner and caused accident to the motor cyclist and motor cyclist succumbed to the injuries as pleaded in the petition?

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

Smt. Preeti Shashank, learned counsel appearing for the appellant-KSRTC submitted that the Tribunal arbitrarily fixed the entire liability against the driver of the respondent though the insured bus was not responsible for the accident in question.

The Tribunal has failed to notice the fact that the rider of the motorcycle and the pillion rider had consumed alcohol as shown in the charge sheet and also the Forensic Science Laboratory report Exhibits P17 and P18.

The rider of the motorcycle drove the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the KSRTC Bus and the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the deceased- Manjunath and not due to the negligent act on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus, but a false case was registered against the driver of the KSRTC bus.
It is further submitted that the Tribunal has failed to consider the evidence of CW1 in CC No.390 of 2020.
The Tribunal has not properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and on all these grounds sought to allow the appeals.

On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-claimants supports the impugned judgment and award and submits that the Tribunal, after considering the oral and documentary evidence placed before it, has awarded the just compensation which does not call for any interference.

14. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, the following questions would arise for our consideration in these appeals:
1.
Whether the appellant-Insurance Company has made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the Insurance Company?
2. What order or award?

Regarding Point No.1:

sentences.text: We have carefully examined the material placed before this Court.
In both cases, the Tribunal has assigned - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11019-DB reasons to issues No.1 to 4.

At paragraph 13 of its judgment, the Tribunal has observed thus:
"13. Issue No.1 to 4 in both the petitions: The accident in question is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that motor cyclist and pillion rider both are succumbed to the injuries.
According to petitioners the driver of the bus was responsible for the accident, but according to respondents motor cyclist himself was responsible for the accident.
Admittedly, PW.1 and 2 are not eye witnesses to the accident, but they relied upon the police documents to prove rash or negligent act.
Since petitions are U/s.166 of M.V. Act, the burden heavily lies upon the petitioners to show that the said accident is outcome of the rash or negligent act of the driver of the bus.

Ex.P.1 is the complaint, Ex.P.2 is the FIR, Ex.P.3 is the spot panchanama, Ex.P.4 and 9 are inquest panchanamas, Ex.P.5 and 19 are the P.M. report, Ex.P.6 is the MVI report and Ex.P.7 is the chargesheet.

As per Ex.P.7 chargesheet it is alleged that the driver of the bus was proceeding from Dharwad towards Gabbur and went to his extreme right side and caused the accident to motor cycle and hence, he is responsible for the accident.

It is also alleged that the rider of the motor cycle i.e. Manjunath S/o. Ganesh Shinde and pillion rider Vinayak Vishwanath Annigeri both were drunk and Manjunah was riding the motor cycle by drinking alcohol.
Ex.P.17 is FSL report of pillion rider Vinayak Annigeri, which discloses that out of 100 ml blood 51.75 mg Ethyl alcohol was found in his body.
Ex . P.18
FSL report with respect to rider of the motor cycle Manjunath discloses that 64.80 mg Ethyl alcohol was found out of 100 ml blood.

So,
motor cyclist was riding his motor cycle in drunken state of mind.
The time of accident is night 12.45 a.m.
Though it is alleged that KSRTC driver alone is responsible for the accident, but evidence on record discloses that motor cyclist is also equally responsible for the accident.
The accident was head on collusion.

So,
considering the nature of the accident, time of the accident and considering the fact that motor cyclist was riding his motor cycle in drunken state of mind, I hold that the driver of the bus is responsible for negligence to the extent of 50% and motor cyclist was responsible for rest 50%.
PW.2 mother of the deceased was suggested by - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11019-DB counsel for respondent No.2 that her son was not holding D.L. but she denied it.
She tried to contend that her son was holding D.L., but she admitted that it was not produced before the court.
So, deceased motor cyclist was not holding D.L.
She denied the suggestion that her son alone was responsible for the accident.
Chargesheet is filed against driver of the bus, petitioners have not impleaded motor cyclist and its owner as parties.

But there is a contributory The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Smt Renuka W/O Ganesh Shinde on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64960345/
8 negligence on the motor cyclist also.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Smt Renuka W/O Ganesh Shinde
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention of respondent No.2 that the driver of the bus was acquitted by the criminal court ad hence, there was no negligence at all cannot be accepted.

It was also argued that there was no eye witness to the accident, but police have falsely implicated the bus, but driver of the bus has not taken any steps to lodge complaint against deceased persons stating that motor cyclist alone was responsible for the accident.
So, evidence on record discloses that the driver of the bus as well as motor cyclist are equally responsible for the accident.

Hence, I answer issue No.1 to 4 in partly Affirmative."
17.
On re-appreciation of evidence on record, we do not find any legal infirmities/illegalities in the finding given by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts.
Hence, we answer the point No.1 in the negative.

Whether the appellant-Insurance Company has made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the Insurance Company?
2. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Smt. Preeti Shashank, learned counsel appearing for the appellant-KSRTC submitted that the Tribunal arbitrarily fixed the entire liability against the driver of the respondent though the insured bus was not responsible for the accident in question.
The Tribunal has failed to notice the fact that the rider of the motorcycle and the pillion rider had consumed alcohol as shown in the charge sheet and also the Forensic Science Laboratory report Exhibits P17 and P18.
The rider of the motorcycle drove the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the KSRTC Bus and the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the deceased- Manjunath and not due to the negligent act on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus, but a false case was registered against the driver of the KSRTC bus.
The Tribunal has not properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and on all these grounds sought to allow the appeals.
On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-claimants supports the impugned judgment and award and submits that the Tribunal, after considering the oral and documentary evidence placed before it, has awarded the just compensation which does not call for any interference.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS: The Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts.
opennyai_summary.decision: Hence, we answer the point No.1 in the negative.

llm_case_outcome.decision_text: Hence, we answer the point No.1 in the negative.
